one_line: Last Paramara-era ruler Mahalakadeva and his minister-general Goga, facing the Delhi Sultanate’s conquest of Malwa (1305–1310 CE).

appearance.age_look: Mahalakadeva appears in his late 30s, lean and regal; Goga in his mid-40s, broader and battle-hardened.
appearance.face: Mahalakadeva has an oval face, medium-brown Malwa complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache with a calm yet strained default expression; Goga has a squarer jaw, slightly darker complexion, thicker moustache, close-cropped beard, a faint scar on his left cheek, and a focused, determined gaze.
appearance.hair: Mahalakadeva’s hair is dark brown, shoulder-length, parted in the middle and tied back low, mostly concealed under a muted gold cloth turban with a simple red band; Goga’s hair is dark, shorter and tied in a small knot at the back, under a plain deep-red cloth turban without ornament.
appearance.costume: Both wear early-14th-century central Indian court-appropriate garments: Mahalakadeva in a knee-length, side-tied cotton angarkha in soft off-white with a narrow red border and faint block-printed floral motifs, over a deep-red silk uttariya shawl draped over his left shoulder and across the torso, and loose off-white churidar-style trousers gathered at the ankles above simple brown leather shoes; he has a narrow gold kamarbandh belt, modest gold stud earrings, a single thin gold armlet on the right arm, and a small tilak mark at the forehead. Goga wears a more martial version: a quilted cotton coat (gamcha/ padded coat) in dull indigo with visible vertical stitching and a slightly flared skirt to just above the knee, over a plain off-white tunic, deep-olive fitted trousers, and sturdy dark-brown leather boots; over his coat he has a broad dark-brown leather belt with a simple brass buckle and a secondary cloth sash in faded red, with minimal jewellery (only a thin iron bangle on his right wrist) and a practical, no-nonsense appearance.
appearance.signature: Mahalakadeva carries a sheathed straight-edged steel sword with a simple Indo-Islamic style crossguard and plain disc pommel at his left hip, held by his gold kamarbandh; Goga holds a long, slightly curved steel talwar with a plain iron hilt and small knuckle-guard, the blade showing subtle use-wear, and a round, slightly dented iron shield strapped across his back.

ref_desc: Mahalakadeva is a lean, medium-brown man with an oval face, short beard, shoulder-length dark hair under a muted gold turban, wearing an off-white patterned angarkha, red shawl and churidar with a sheathed straight sword, beside broader, darker Goga in an indigo quilted coat, red turban, olive trousers, boots, and carrying a curved talwar and round iron shield, all in off-white, deep red, indigo, olive and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two historically grounded early-14th-century Malwa figures standing side by side: Mahalakadeva is a lean, medium-brown man with an oval face, calm but strained expression, short neat beard and moustache, and shoulder-length dark hair tied back under a muted gold cloth turban with a simple red band; he wears a knee-length off-white cotton angarkha with a narrow red border and faint floral block-print motifs, a deep-red silk shawl draped over his left shoulder and across his torso, loose off-white churidar-style trousers gathered at the ankles, and simple brown leather shoes, with a narrow gold belt, modest gold stud earrings, a thin gold armlet on his right arm, and a small tilak on his forehead, his straight-edged steel sword sheathed at his left hip. Beside him, Goga is a broader, slightly darker man in his mid-40s with a squarer jaw, faint scar on his left cheek, thick moustache, close-cropped beard, and focused gaze, his shorter dark hair tied in a small knot under a plain deep-red turban; he wears a dull indigo quilted cotton coat with vertical stitching down to above the knee over a plain off-white tunic, deep-olive fitted trousers, and sturdy dark-brown leather boots, with a wide brown leather belt and a faded red cloth sash, minimal jewellery save a thin iron bangle, and he grips a long slightly curved steel talwar with a plain iron hilt while a round slightly dented iron shield is strapped across his back, all rendered in a consistent palette of off-white, deep red, indigo blue, olive green and brown leather tones.
